rules.sentence: The most common indication of GIBS is for a GI bleed that especially involving mid and lower GI tracts.
It can detect GIB at a rate as low as 0.1mL/ml.[18][19]
GIBS should not be used for chronic occult bleeds.
Diagnostic criteria for a positive GI bleeding scan include all of the following:
Considerable bowel bleeding is identifiable with its linear pattern and peripheral location in the abdomen.
Sigmoid bleed scan appears as S-shaped.
Small bowel bleed can be differentiated with its rapid curvilinear pattern of activity and central location.
Factors associated with low bleeding include; detection of activity after one hour, low target to background ratio (less intense than liver), and short bleeding duration.
Factors indicating higher bleeding rates include early and intense activity with longer durations.[18]
